title: Adopt $\neq$ Adapt: Longitudinal Analyses of LLM Conversations in the Wild
abstract: arXiv:2605.29018v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Although a growing body of research has begun to describe user--LLM interactions, the picture it paints is largely static; little is known about how individual users change their behavior over time. To address this gap, we analyze the conversational trajectories of ~12,000 randomly sampled Microsoft Bing Copilot users and compare these with data from WildChat-4.8M. While the Copilot data contains significant population-level trends, we find that trends in individual user trajectories are much weaker; user habits prove to be overwhelmingly sticky. We also find stark differences between users of different activity levels: more active users have more successful conversations and use the LLM for more complex and professionally oriented tasks. translated_title: 采用 ≠ 适应：真实场景中大语言模型对话的纵向分析
translated_abstract: 尽管越来越多的研究开始描述用户与大语言模型之间的交互，但这些研究所描绘的图景在很大程度上是静态的；我们对于个体用户的行为如何随时间变化知之甚少。为了填补这一空白，我们分析了约12,000名随机抽样的微软Bing Copilot用户的对话轨迹，并将其与WildChat-4.8M数据集进行比较。虽然Copilot数据中存在显著的群体层面趋势，但我们发现个体用户轨迹中的趋势要弱得多；用户习惯被证明具有极强的粘性。我们还发现不同活跃程度的用户之间存在明显差异：更活跃的用户拥有更多成功的对话，并将大语言模型用于更复杂、更面向职业的任务。一些用户趋势也出现在WildChat-4.8M中，但我们发现有证据表明该数据集明显偏向高度熟练的“高级”用户。最终，我们的结果表明，现有的……
tldr: 该论文通过对约1.2万名Bing Copilot用户进行纵向分析，首次揭示了“采用”不等于“适应”：群体层面趋势显著但个体用户习惯极其粘滞，且现有公开数据集严重偏向高级用户，无法代表普通用户的真实使用行为。
en_tdlr: Through longitudinal analysis of ~12,000 Bing Copilot users, this paper shows that adoption does not equal adaptation: while population-level trends are significant, individual user habits are overwhelmingly sticky, and existing datasets like WildChat are heavily skewed toward power users, failing to represent ordinary users' real-world behavior.
